ports.label: USB-C (entrada de energia)
ports.note: a fonte deve poder entregar 2 A mesmo com o consumo médio em 440 mA

ports.label: 5V / GND (header GPIO)
ports.src: communications.gpio-header.layout (Raspberry Pi compatible: 5 V nos pinos 2 e 4, GND nos pinos 6, 9, 14, 20, 25, 30, 34 e 39); input-voltage 5 V
ports.note: entrada alternativa ao USB-C, pelos pinos de 5 V do header de 40 pinos (que NÃO vem soldado de fábrica). Use UMA entrada de energia: ligar USB-C e header juntos é bloqueado pela validação

ports.label: USB0 (Type-C, OTG)
ports.note: Device (OTG) por padrão, pode virar Host via orangepi-config. Existe uma segunda porta de dados, USB1 (ver porta "usb1"), fixa em modo Host — corrige o que estava registrado antes (só 1 porta USB de dados)

ports.label: USB1 (Type-C, Host)
ports.note: sempre em modo Host, não precisa configurar nada — melhor porta para periféricos fixos (câmera, ESP32, etc.)

ports.label: Header GPIO 40 pinos
ports.note: compatível com Raspberry Pi, mas NÃO vem soldado de fábrica

ports.label: UART (no header)
ports.note: 5 instâncias: UART0 e UART5 em pinos dedicados; UART2, UART3 e UART4 dividem pino com I²C (TWI0/TWI2) ou PWM (PWM3/PWM4) — só uma função por vez nesses pinos

ports.label: I²C (no header)
ports.note: 3 barramentos: TWI1 em pinos dedicados; TWI0 e TWI2 dividem pino com UART2 e UART3 respectivamente

ports.label: SPI (no header)
ports.note: 1 barramento SPI1 (MOSI/MISO/CLK dedicados) com 2 chip-selects (CS0, CS1) — até 2 dispositivos escravos no mesmo barramento

ports.label: PWM (no header)
ports.note: PWM hardware via pwmchip0 (kernel), desabilitado por padrão. PWM1/PWM2 em pinos dedicados; PWM3/PWM4 dividem pino com UART4. Frequência máxima não publicada (manual só demonstra teste a 50 Hz)

wireless.wifi: IEEE 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac, dual band 2.4 GHz / 5 GHz, onboard antenna

gpio-header.layout: Raspberry Pi compatible, unpopulated (header not soldered from factory)

uart-instances.list: UART0 (PH0 TX pin 8 / PH1 RX pin 10, dedicated), UART5 (PH2 TX pin 11 / PH3 RX pin 13, dedicated), UART2 (PI5 TX pin 15 / PI6 RX pin 22, shares pins with TWI0), UART3 (PI9 TX pin 28 / PI10 RX pin 27, shares pins with TWI2), UART4 (PI13 TX pin 7 / PI14 RX pin 16, shares pins with PWM3/PWM4)
uart-instances.note: UART2, UART3 and UART4 each share their pins with an I2C (TWI) or PWM function — only one of the multiplexed functions can be used at a time on those pins. UART0 and UART5 are dedicated.
uart-instances.src: user manual v1.1 section 3.17 (40 pin interface pin description)

i2c-instances.list: TWI1 (SDA pin 3 / SCL pin 5, dedicated), TWI0 (SCL/UART2_TX pin 15, SDA/UART2_RX pin 22, shares pins with UART2), TWI2 (SDA/UART3_RX pin 27, SCL/UART3_TX pin 28, shares pins with UART3)

spi-instances.description: SPI1: MOSI pin 19 / MISO pin 21 / CLK pin 23 (dedicated), plus two chip-selects CS0 pin 24 and CS1 pin 26, allowing up to 2 slave devices on the same bus

pwm-instances.type: hardware PWM via kernel pwmchip0, disabled by default (must be enabled with orangepi-config)
pwm-instances.list: PWM1 (PI11, pin 32, dedicated), PWM2 (PI12, pin 33, dedicated), PWM3 (PI13, pin 7, shares pins with UART4_TX), PWM4 (PI14, pin 16, shares pins with UART4_RX)
pwm-instances.note: manual only demonstrates a 50 Hz test output (period set via /sys/class/pwm/pwmchip0/pwmN/period in ns); maximum output frequency is not published

usb.role: power input or data; Device mode (OTG) by default, switchable to Host mode via orangepi-config
power input or data; fixed Host mode

communications.usb-note: both Type-C connectors can supply power and both can carry USB2.0 data; USB0 defaults to Device mode (e.g. for flashing) and USB1 is always Host — a USB Type-A device needs USB1 directly or USB0 switched to Host mode

expansion-connector.description: optional expansion board adds 100M ethernet, 2x USB 2.0 type-A, IR receiver, audio out, TV out and power button

thermal-zones.note: SoC junction/critical shutdown temperature per thermal zone, not an ambient operating temperature rating (still unpublished — see componentes_TODO.md)
thermal-zones.src: user manual v1.1 section 3.16.2 (linux 6.1 `sensors` output, crit = +110.0°C per zone)
